reply.thought: Before any payout, I need to verify the refunds table matches what Alpha reported. Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly, so I can proceed. Next I need the list of orders to identify the customers to pay.

The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the orders cover three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance before recording any payout, starting with acme.
The acme net balance of 48125 checks out against its orders (31647 + 31611) minus its refund (15133). Next I need birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 54597 matches its orders (38685 + 35281 = 73966) minus its refunds (12701 + 6668 = 19369). Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 46961 matches its orders (32516 + 14445) with no refunds, so all three balances reconcile and the refunds match Alpha's report. Recording the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout went through. Birch and cobalt remain, and both balances already reconciled against their orders and refunds, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt is the last customer. Its net balance of 46961 reconciled against its orders with no refunds, so I'll record its payout now.
All three payouts recorded successfully after the refunds matched Alpha's report and each balance reconciled against its orders and refunds. Reporting the final payouts.
